newsitem.title: USA: IPO VIEW - Sparks should fly in IPO market this week.
newsitem.headline: IPO VIEW - Sparks should fly in IPO market this week.

text.p: Only a handful of companies are on deck to go public this week, but many are considered cream-of-the-crop offerings, which could drive already robust demand even higher, analysts say.
The companies come from a wide spectrum, including a Chinese airline, a renovator of offshore drilling rigs, a publisher of technology magazines, a European denim supplier and two travel companies.

"The market has really changed dramatically from a couple of months ago. Activity is up significantly and strong after-market perfomance is encouraging even more investors to get into IPOs," said Bob Levitt, managing director at Credit Suisse First Boston.

The rising broad market, which continues to smash records, has also added to the atmosphere for IPOs because investors, flush with cash, are more willing to take chances with riskier companies, IPO analysts said.
But the rising market can be a double-edged sword.
"As you approach the 8,000 level, you get a more skittish investor base that thinks the market might be overvalued," Levitt said.

About six very strong deals are in the works this week. The two biggest deals this week are a $688 million offering by electronics reservations company Galileo International Inc and a $565 million deal by China Southern Airlines Co Ltd For much of this year, investors have shown a preference for large, highly liquid offerings.

Galileo, which analysts say could easily jump over three points, gives travel agencies around the world access to the reservation systems of 525 airlines, 48 car rental companies and 200 major hotel chains. It completed more than 300 bookings in 1996 representing about $50 billion in travel services, according to its prospectus.
China Southern is called an H-share listing -- a China-incorporated company to be listed in Hong Kong. It will also offer shares on the New York Stock Exchange.

But a smaller offering, Freide Goldman International Inc, might eclipse both deals with scorching gains. Analysts are predicting a stock jump of at least 3 points and one said he would not be surprised by much higher gains.

Underwriters have already raised terms to $70 million from an earlier estimate of about $54 million. The company converts, retrofits and repairs offshore rigs and just got into the new market to convert offshore drilling units and tankers into deepwater floating storage vessels.

Three other deals are attracting mobs of investors as well, IPO analysts say. Vince Slavin, who tracks IPOs for Cantor Fitzgerald says Novel Denim Holdings Ltd, Travel Services International and CMP Media Inc could all surge when the stocks open for trade.
Novel Denim Holdings supplies denim fabric and garments to Tommy Hilfiger, Wrangler, Pepe Jeans, Lee, the Gap and others.
CMP Media Inc, whose stable of magazines and newspapers include Information Week, Communications Week and Electronic Engineering Times, plans to raise about $90 million.
"Last week was a great week -- there were only a handful of deals, but they did well. This week should be the same," said John Fitzgibbon, editor of the IPO Aftermarket.
